headline: The recording device that the US Justice Department says an OpenAI employee hid in a conference room appears to be a $13.99 thumbnail-sized camera and microphone.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a wry price-tag angle on a serious case already covered elsewhere.
importance_line: It shows how cheaply a meeting room can be bugged, which matters to AI labs guarding unreleased work, but the claims are allegations and the device model is Gizmodo's reading of the department's materials.
summary: Gizmodo reports that, judging by the US Justice Department's press materials, the device an OpenAI employee is accused of hiding in a San Francisco conference room is a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, a thumbnail-sized microphone and camera sold for $13.99, which OpenAI called a "sophisticated recording device". Gizmodo notes its camera is only 2 megapixels, that it could send data over Wi-Fi, and that OpenAI says it used its own AI models to analyse the device's data to find the suspect, while the case so far rests on the department's allegations.
notes: Read from fulltext. Same case as the AP entry C13-02; this is the lighter Gizmodo angle (price and specs). Accused deliberately not named.
